basis: NIST assurance-case practice: an auditable artifact linking claims, systematic arguments, explicit assumptions, and underlying evidence.
invariant: A claim states the property believed to hold.
A mechanism attempts to create that property.
Evidence supports or falsifies the claim.
An assessment determines whether the evidence is sufficient.

rules: A claim may not skip states.
OPERATIONAL requires every readiness gate in assessment_readiness.json to be true.
INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED requires a reviewer who did not author the mechanism.
EVIDENCED requires BOTH positive and negative (falsification) tests that actually run.
A mechanism change without a claim-version increment forces REGRESSED.

claims.claim: The published commitment does not reveal a low-entropy inject package before opening.

mechanism.construction: SHA-384(frame(domain, canonical_package, opening_salt))

assumptions: The opening salt remains confidential until reveal.
The CSPRNG provides the required entropy.
Canonicalization is deterministic.
SHA-384 remains suitable for the stated purpose.
limitations: Hiding fails if opening material is disclosed before reveal.
This construction does not conceal package length unless separately padded.
claims.status_note: Cannot reach INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED until an EA performer exists (readiness gate 'exercise_assurance_operational' is PENDING).

claims.claim: Exercise Assurance cannot substitute a different inject package after publishing the commitment.

mechanism.construction: Digest over the length-framed preimage including the canonical package; supersession requires a new signed commitment chained to the prior one.

assumptions: SHA-384 collision resistance holds.
Canonicalization is deterministic.
Both commitments remain published on supersession.
limitations: Binding is to the canonical serialization, not to intent. A semantically equivalent repackaging produces a different digest and must be superseded explicitly.

claims.claim: The Red Team can execute an authorized assessment but cannot produce a valid authorization for it.

mechanism.construction: The encrypted Ed25519 authorization private key is held by the White approval authority. Aegis refuses to run without a receipt verifying against a separately pinned trust key.

assumptions: The authorization private key is not accessible to Red. NOT YET ESTABLISHED - readiness gate 'key_custody_verified' is PENDING.
IAM denies Red access to the key material.
Operators cannot obtain the signing password.
claims.evidence_gap: No test attempts authorization AS RED and asserts denial. Custody is currently procedural, not demonstrated.
limitations: Holds only while key custody holds. A signing key on an operator machine voids this claim entirely.
claims.status_note: The mechanism exists in code. The claim is NOT evidenced: nobody has attempted to authorize as Red and been denied.

claims.claim: The sealed Aegis audit ledger is evidence independent of the operator who produced it.

mechanism.construction: Domain-separated Ed25519 authorization and evidence seals use purpose-bound, separately generated keypairs. Both signing and verification reject a key whose purpose metadata does not match the operation.

assumptions: The evidence private key remains outside Red custody.
Purpose metadata and distinct public-key pins are deployed from reviewed configuration.
limitations: The implementation prevents cross-purpose use through its supported API. Host administrators with raw private-key access can bypass application controls; production custody must enforce separation independently.
claims.status_note: Migration step 1 is implemented and falsification-tested. Operational independence still depends on the separate production-custody gate.

claims.claim: The audit chain detects mutation and interior deletion of ledger records.

scope.artifact: Aegis Red Team v0.1.0 AuditLedger; Sentinel Blue evidence store makes an equivalent claim

mechanism.construction: SHA-256 hash chain with exclusive file locking; verify() recomputes and refuses further appends after a break.

assumptions: An attacker cannot rewrite the whole file and recompute the chain undetected. Explicitly out of scope - external anchoring required.
limitations: Does not detect rollback or deletion of the entire store. Both projects state this.
claims.status_note: Positive and falsification tests now cover mutation and interior deletion in both implementations. Whole-store rollback remains explicitly excluded and requires external anchoring.

claims.claim: A source-review check cannot follow a symbolic link outside the authorized root.

mechanism.construction: Path resolution constrained to the authorized root; links escaping it are rejected.

assumptions: The test executes on every supported platform.
limitations: The Windows falsification uses an NTFS directory junction because it exercises the reparse-point escape without requiring symbolic-link privilege.
claims.status_note: The falsification test passes on this Windows host without privilege-dependent skips; CI runs it on Windows and Linux with skips forbidden.

claims.claim: Sentinel Blue never performs containment, account disablement, process termination, or blocking; high-risk response requires two approvers.

mechanism.construction: The response module emits plans only; there is no execution path. Unknown response actions fail closed.

assumptions: No downstream integration silently executes an emitted plan.
limitations: Constrains the platform, not the humans or the SOAR tooling that consumes its output.

claims.claim: Sentinel Blue's audit chain is externally anchored by a party that cannot write to it.

scope.artifact: SoD-11 head-hash export to White's evidence manifest

mechanism.construction: Chain head hash exported to White's WORM evidence manifest at each exercise close and monthly.

assumptions: White's manifest is genuinely append-only.
The export actually occurs on cadence.
claims.evidence_gap: Designed, never executed. No exercise has closed and no export has occurred.
limitations: Procedural anchor, weaker than Aegis's cryptographic seal design.

claims.claim: Red is independent from development and from defense operations, and can therefore support CA-8(1) and SA-11(5) where organizational position permits.

mechanism.construction: Reporting lines: Red does not report through Yellow, Orange, or Blue, nor to an engineering manager whose systems it assesses.

assumptions: The reporting lines exist in the instantiated organization. Open Decisions O-1..O-16 are OPEN; no organization has been instantiated.
claims.evidence_gap: No organizational chart exists to verify. The model is parameterized against P2 defaults, not against a real org.
limitations: Does NOT provide independent exercise scoring where Red participated.
Does NOT satisfy external organizational assessment (3PAO / C3PAO / QSA).
CA-2(1) applicability depends on assessment context and the authorizing authority.
Applicability is determined PER SYSTEM and is not inherited globally.
claims.status_note: v1 of this claim was overbroad ('Red closes F-1') and was withdrawn 2026-08-14.

claims.claim: No result may be presented as assurance while any readiness gate is false.

mechanism.construction: claim_check.py evaluates the gates and exits non-zero; CI blocks on a non-zero exit.

assumptions: The protected assessment-issuance workflow remains required and cannot be bypassed by repository administrators.
limitations: Enforces marking and exit status; cannot prevent a human from copying a number into a slide.
claims.status_note: The dedicated assessment-issuance workflow now invokes --require-ready and fails while readiness is false. Branch protection remains an external deployment prerequisite.

claims.claim: Exercise scope, procedures, telemetry expectations, detection expectations, rollback state, readiness snapshot, rubric, and role-trust registry are content-addressed and immutable after freeze.

mechanism.construction: Strict canonical exercise-plan/1.0 serialization and SHA-256 digest stored with the exact plan JSON; every transition revalidates the digest.

assumptions: SHA-256 remains suitable.
Whole-store rollback is handled by an external anchor.
limitations: Content identity is not proof that the approved procedure is safe or effective.

claims.claim: The supported CLI lifecycle boundary rejects unsigned, tampered, stale, role-mismatched, plan-mismatched, and replayed transitions.

mechanism.construction: Exact signed envelope binds plan digest, states, actor, role, reason, nonce, key ID, and a maximum five-minute validity window to a role public key in the registry whose digest is pinned by the frozen plan.

assumptions: Private keys remain outside the application.
The role trust registry is integrity protected.
System time is trustworthy.
limitations: Direct library callers must provide an equivalently authenticated boundary.
Key custody and IAM denial are external prerequisites.

claims.claim: Evidence and six-stage results cannot be credited to an exercise or test case other than the frozen case they reference.

mechanism.construction: Foreign-keyed evidence records bind exercise ID, frozen test-case ID, producer, media type, artifact digest, and collection time; result insertion verifies same-case ownership.

assumptions: Evidence content hashes are computed over the preserved artifact.
Producer identities are authenticated by the deployment boundary.
limitations: A digest proves byte identity, not truth, independence, or collection completeness.

claims.claim: A configured automatic failure forces the final score to zero before aggregation, and missing evidence prevents scoring.

mechanism.construction: Exact component matching, mandatory evidence lists, strict numeric types, weight-sum validation, and auto-fail evaluation precede pass calculation.

assumptions: The frozen rubric represents the approved governance decision.
Exercise Assurance validates evidence quality separately.
limitations: The scorer cannot prevent a human from copying a diagnostic value into an unauthorized presentation.

claims.claim: The live Aegis Purple store detects transition mutation, interior deletion, tail deletion, and modification of exercise, evidence, result, or replay state relative to stored integrity roots.

mechanism.construction: Sequence-numbered SHA-256 transition chain with predecessor hashes and transactional head/count metadata, plus a canonical state root over exercises, evidence, results, and consumed nonces.

assumptions: The complete database is not rolled back as a unit.
SQLite durability settings are honored by the filesystem.
limitations: Whole-store rollback requires publication of export_anchor() to a separately administered append-only witness.

claims.claim: An exercise cannot start unless authorization, mode, revocation status, and all eleven safety boundaries hold.

mechanism.construction: Registry- and role-verified Ed25519 authorization and environment-attestation signatures, mode gating against readiness gates, revocation checks at preflight and four runner safety boundaries, and per-boundary field checks.

assumptions: The readiness config reflects real gate state.
Production trust-store enrollment and custody are truthful external inputs.
limitations: The formal path is engineering-tested with ephemeral production-role keys; no real production authority is enrolled.

claims.claim: run_rehearsal.py cannot execute directly, cannot reuse an old clearance, and cannot execute modified inputs; it proceeds only with a valid short-lived clearance from a trusted, non-revoked authorization.

mechanism.construction: Clearance signed over a domain-separated payload binding exercise id, mode, authorization digest, manifest digest, approved scope, authorization expiry, revocation-list digest, safety-boundary digest, issue/expiry times, single-use nonce, and runner identity. The runner verifies it independently and consumes the nonce. InvalidSignature is caught specifically and fails closed.

assumptions: The clearance signing key is not accessible to whoever runs the runner. NOT ESTABLISHED - readiness gate 'key_custody_verified' is PENDING.
Trust-store records establish signer identity; a valid signature from an unknown key is unauthorized.
limitations: Defends against accidental bypass, replay, and modified inputs. Does NOT defend against host-level access to the clearance signing key.
Engineering mode is cleared by a TEST_ONLY fixture issuer; the real production trust store remains empty.
Replay protection is PER HOST: the nonce ledger is machine-local and gitignored (see EXERCISE-NONCE-LEDGER-001).

claims.claim: A Red execution receipt is a separate signed object bound to the authorization fingerprint and attempted test cases.

mechanism.construction: Domain-separated Ed25519 receipt with exact fields for exercise, authorization digest, test cases, action digest, timestamps, and Red execution key.

assumptions: The enrolled Red execution key remains distinct from authorization keys.
limitations: A receipt proves what its signer attested, not that every action was captured.

claims.claim: Only an enrolled Exercise Assurance or Internal Audit key can sign a complete assessment result through the supported verifier.

mechanism.construction: Role-restricted domain-separated signature binds scorecard, evidence manifest, completeness, scores, marking, and issue time.

assumptions: Exercise Assurance key custody and independence hold externally.
limitations: Engineering tests do not instantiate an independent human assessor.

claims.claim: A revocation becoming effective during execution halts the runner at the next material safety boundary.

mechanism.construction: The runner re-evaluates exercise/key revocations before baseline, after baseline, before retest, and before evidence write.

assumptions: The revocation feed is available and integrity-protected.
limitations: A blocking host failure between boundaries is handled by the independent STOP mechanism.

claims.claim: The lifecycle validator refuses incomplete or mismatched rotation and recovery evidence for the five program key purposes.

mechanism.construction: Exact five-purpose records require distinct old/new fingerprints, recovered-current equality, valid chronology, and holder-unavailable exercise.

assumptions: Submitted fingerprints were captured from the actual custody system.
limitations: The validator cannot perform an HSM recovery; A5 supplies operational evidence.

claims.claim: The fixed Red registry includes a bounded offline check for unpinned dependencies and write-all workflow permissions.

mechanism.construction: Resolved-root-constrained traversal, file/finding budgets, fixed manifest selection, and static dependency/workflow rules.

assumptions: Repository manifests use supported formats.
limitations: This check does not replace SCA, provenance verification, or workflow semantic review.

claims.claim: The assurance-issuance workflow cannot pass while a readiness gate is false; only engineering CI may pass under an explicit hold.

mechanism.construction: assessment-issuance.yml must contain --require-ready and must NOT contain --allow-not-ready; no workflow may combine both. Asserted by test, not by convention.

assumptions: CI runs the guard test. NOTE: as of 2026-08-14 the program is UNTRACKED and no workflow has ever executed; the guard currently runs via the local runner (run_ci.py).
Workflow files are the authoritative CI definition.
evidence: falsification: injecting --allow-not-ready into assessment-issuance.yml FAILS 2 tests (verified 2026-08-14)
limitations: Guards the workflow files only. A runner configured outside these files, or a manually dispatched job, is not covered.
Cannot prevent a human running the validator locally and quoting the result.
Corrected 2026-08-14: v1 asserted CI enforcement while the workflows sat at a nested path GitHub Actions never reads. The separation is now guarded at the repository root and by the local runner.

claims.claim: Fixture private keys and commitment opening material exist on disk for engineering use but can never enter version control.

mechanism.construction: .gitignore excludes *_fixture_private_keys.json, *.pem, *.key, *_private*.json, opening material, and nonce ledgers. A test asserts the keys are ignored AND that no secret-shaped file is tracked.

assumptions: Contributors commit from within this repository rather than copying files elsewhere.
limitations: Guards this repository only. A file copied into another repo is not covered.
Cannot retroactively remove a secret already committed elsewhere.

claims.claim: The program's CI gates are executable: reachable by GitHub Actions when pushed, and runnable locally without any external service.

mechanism.construction: A path-scoped workflow at the REPOSITORY ROOT (GitHub reads only <repo-root>/.github/workflows/), plus a local runner executing the same nine gates. A test asserts the root workflow exists and actually invokes the gates.

assumptions: The repository is eventually pushed to a host that executes Actions. Until then only the local runner provides enforcement.
evidence: local run 2026-08-14: 9/9 engineering gates PASS; --assurance FAILS closed (exit 1)
GitHub Actions run 31817937014 SUCCESS on ubuntu-latest AND windows-latest (2026-08-14) - the workflow has now actually executed
limitations: Local runner enforcement depends on a human invoking it; it is not a pre-commit hook.
The previously claimed CI enforcement (2026-08-14, earlier) was unevidenced: workflows sat at a nested path Actions never reads.
Executed and green as of run 31817937014. Runs 31817114551 and 31817758247 FAILED first, which is what surfaced the reproducibility and line-ending defects.

claims.claim: The local runner and the GitHub workflow cannot drift: both derive from one gate manifest, and CI is pinned against supply-chain substitution.

mechanism.construction: Single manifest consumed by run_ci.py; tests assert the root workflow covers every manifest gate, pins all actions to 40-char SHAs, and installs dependencies with --require-hashes.

assumptions: Contributors add gates to the manifest rather than only to one runner.
limitations: Guards the workflow file, not the runner host.
Does not verify the pinned SHAs correspond to the intended action releases.

claims.claim: The replay ledger cannot grow without bound, and cannot silently lose replay protection.

mechanism.construction: Entries older than 24x the clearance TTL are pruned (such clearances are already refused by the expiry check); unparsable entries are retained rather than discarded; a corrupt ledger fails closed; a hard entry ceiling refuses rather than degrading.

assumptions: Host clock is not adjusted backwards by more than the retention margin.
limitations: The ledger is machine-local and gitignored: replay protection is PER HOST. A clearance replayed on a different host is not blocked. Cross-host protection needs a shared ledger and is a deployment decision.
Pruning assumes a monotonic-enough clock.

claims.claim: Content-addressed files hash identically on Linux and Windows checkouts, and the harness provisions itself from a clean clone.

mechanism.construction: `* text=auto eol=lf` plus `-text` (no translation) on files hashed or signed over raw bytes; fixture trust material and engineering scaffolding generated on demand rather than committed.

assumptions: Contributors do not override core.autocrlf per-file.
Generated fixture material is TEST_ONLY and cannot satisfy formal mode.
evidence: GitHub Actions run 31817937014: SUCCESS on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest
GitHub Actions run 31817758247: windows-latest FAILED with 'rule integrity check failed: endpoint.json' before the fix (NEGATIVE)
GitHub Actions run 31817114551: FAILED on missing fixture keys in a fresh clone before the fix (NEGATIVE)
local fresh-clone simulation: fixture material deleted, 10/10 gates PASS
GitHub Actions run 31818720772: macos-latest FAILED at hash-pinned install, demonstrating the pin is enforced rather than decorative (NEGATIVE)
limitations: Guards the files listed in .gitattributes. A new content-addressed file added without an entry is not covered.

macOS is NOT exercised. Attempted 2026-08-14 (run 31818720772): the reviewed hash-pinned runtime covers CPython 3.12 x64 Linux/Windows wheels only, so --require-hashes refused on macos-latest. Closing this requires REVIEWING and adding macOS wheel hashes to tools/requirements-runtime.txt - not pasting fetched hashes into a file whose purpose is 'exact reviewed runtime'.

claims.claim: An exercise score cannot be marked ASSESSMENT_CANDIDATE, and assurance cannot be permitted, while any readiness gate is unverified in the program's own registry.

mechanism.construction: Readiness is DERIVED from the canonical assessment_readiness.json located from the package's own path. There is no caller-supplied readiness boolean, and a non-canonical registry path is refused outright. Only the exact status string VERIFIED counts; a malformed registry raises rather than defaulting to ready. The result records the derivation source, the pending gates, and digests of both artifacts.

assumptions: Edits to the canonical registry are reviewable and version-controlled.
An attacker with write access to the repository's own registry is out of scope for this control - that edit is visible in git.
limitations: Does not defend against an attacker who can edit the canonical registry in the repository. That edit is version-controlled and reviewable, which is the control at that layer.

v1 of this fix was INSUFFICIENT: it replaced a caller-controlled boolean with a caller-controlled path, and a self-consistent forged registry still produced ASSESSMENT_CANDIDATE. Found by attacking the fix rather than trusting it.

claims.claim: A clearance nonce can be consumed at most once on a given host, including when multiple processes attempt consumption simultaneously.

mechanism.construction: Cross-platform exclusive advisory lock (msvcrt.locking / fcntl.flock) held across the entire read-modify-write of the nonce ledger, with the updated ledger written via a unique fsynced temp file and atomic replace.
mechanism.failure_mode_closed: Concurrent readers previously all observed 'nonce absent' and all wrote.

assumptions: The filesystem honours the platform advisory lock used.
All consumers use this code path; nothing writes the ledger directly.
Participating processes run on the same host and see the same ledger file.
evidence: exercise/tests/test_concurrency.py::NonceRaceTests::test_concurrent_consume_admits_exactly_one_winner (NEGATIVE - 5 of 6 processes consumed the same nonce with the lock removed)
limitations: Replay protection is HOST-LOCAL. Two hosts with separate ledgers can each consume the same nonce; that requires a shared transactional store and is a deployment decision.
Advisory locking does not constrain a process that bypasses this code path or has write access to the ledger.
Verified at 12 workers x 25 rounds on Windows and in CI on Linux; not a proof for arbitrary concurrency.
regression_triggers: Any change to consume(), the ledger format, or the lock helper.
Any new writer of the nonce ledger.
Moving clearance validation to a multi-host deployment.
claims.status_note: Reported as a Medium error-handling defect; measurement showed replay protection did not hold at all under concurrency (3 of 6 processes succeeded on the same nonce, 12/12 rounds). Fix is falsification-verified: removing the lock restores the failure.

claims.claim: Offline source and repository-posture scans read only files inside the authorized root, including when a local attacker swaps a path between validation and read.

mechanism.construction: no-follow bounded traversal + descriptor-inode binding: os.walk(followlinks=False) with realpath containment per component, then open(O_NOFOLLOW) and fstat(descriptor) compared against the traversal-time lstat before any content is read
mechanism.traversal: os.walk(followlinks=False) with realpath containment on every component, covering symlinks, junctions and mounts; bounded by an explicit entry limit that raises rather than truncating.
mechanism.read: File opened once with O_NOFOLLOW where available; fstat on the descriptor is compared against the lstat recorded during traversal. A mismatch in (st_dev, st_ino) refuses the read. All content is read from that descriptor, so no second path lookup exists to race.

assumptions: The filesystem reports stable, distinct (st_dev, st_ino) for distinct files.
realpath resolution is accurate at traversal time.
The scanner process is not itself compromised.
evidence: red-team/tests/test_scan_race.py::ReadVerifiedTests::test_symlink_swapped_in_is_refused (NEGATIVE - skips without symlink privilege, runs in Linux CI)
limitations: The containment decision is time-of-check; the inode binding is what makes it hold at time-of-use. A root directory itself replaced before traversal begins is out of scope for this control.

The symlink-swap evidence skips on Windows hosts without SeCreateSymbolicLink privilege; it executes in Linux CI. The race-injection tests fall back to a real file replacement and run on every platform.
Does not defend against an attacker who can modify file contents in place without changing the inode.
regression_triggers: Any change to safe_scan.py or to how the scanners enumerate or read files.
Adding a new PATH-target check that does its own traversal.
Python version changes affecting os.walk or realpath symlink/junction semantics.
claims.status_note: Closes the external assessment's residual High. Falsification-verified: removing the inode binding makes both end-to-end scanner tests read out-of-scope content.
